Legged robots have the ability to adapt their walking posture to navigate confined spaces due to their high degrees of freedom. However, this has not been exploited in most common approaches to walking planning for robots, which typically use a single robot model. In this paper, we propose a new approach to robot planning that uses models of multiple robots with different postures and gaits in the same planning problem. We show how to apply this approach to the problem of robot motion planning for a humanoid robot that is required to navigate a path in an environment with obstacles. We show that this results in a planner that allows the robot to more effectively adapt to the environment. This work was supported by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) [grant number EPJ0077311].

Muscle mass can inhibit flexibility by pulling harder on connective tissue. Scar tissue can inhibit flexibility by reducing the elasticity of connective tissue. Stretching can increase flexibility over time by lengthening muscles and ligaments. It can also train your body to accommodate deeper stretches. Your body contains feedback mechanisms to prevent your muscles from ripping themselves off of your bones, and these come into play when you are close to the limits of your flexibility. Your muscles also contain mechanisms that prevent them from becoming overextended, which dramatically reduces their strength.

Additionally, some companies are now offering gender-neutral options that are priced the same for all consumers, regardless of gender.

You may spend hours being pushed around by French camera teams, bumped by Italian photographers, or unexpectedly shoved aside by any one of 27 other nations' reporters as the leaders of the European Union make their way through the event, and we desperately try to catch a glimpse of them as they pass by. There will be tense interactions in the press area, stretched necks and raised microphones, as David Cameron arrives at this gathering, which could shape not only his leadership but also the direction of his party and the UK's role globally. Yet, how did the individual—once criticized by the Conservatives for being out of touch over "Europe"—end up in a situation where he has already been advocating for Europe for months and will continue to do so for the next four months? Since making that statement in his initial term as party leader in 2006, there have been three significant shifts that have led him here, a result of his own strategic choices. The simplest reason is that the Conservative Party itself has evolved. After the Maastricht protests failed to secure a public vote in 1993 regarding the treaty that established the modern EU, a faction within the party remained strongly committed to the cause, particularly concerned about the EU's regulations taking precedence over British legislation—sovereignty was a key issue in recent discussions. However, these concerns, though shared by many party members, were not widely accepted within the parliamentary wing of the party; they were balanced, if not overshadowed, by prominent pro-Europhile voices. As the EU expanded and new generations of MPs joined and left, a growing skepticism toward the European project emerged, neither fully supportive nor outright opposed, leading to increased support for a referendum.

A novel technique is introduced for determining the relative positions of location-unaware nodes based on the locations of location-aware nodes and the received signal strength (RSS) measurements between them within a wireless sensor network (WSN). This approach integrates a regularization component into the optimization framework, resulting in enhanced estimation precision even when there are inaccuracies in the known locations of the location-aware nodes or discrepancies in the distances between nodes. The regularization factor is adjusted according to the level of connectivity among the nodes in the network. The method is expressed as a convex optimization problem utilizing the semidefinite relaxation strategy. Comparative experiments with established techniques demonstrate that the proposed method provides significantly more precise node positioning, even when measurement errors are present.

Not a biologist, but how it's been explained to me: Whenever a cell reproduces, the DNA replicates. However, DNA replication is imperfect, and you usually wind up losing some off the ends of the DNA strands. At the end of each strand of DNA are telomeres, which are basically useless bits of genetic code. They serve as kind of a buffer in the replication. As you age, the telomeres get shorter due to imperfect replication, and then once you start losing relevant DNA is when you start to have major bodily breakdowns.

This study explores the operational principles of MixUp by analyzing it through the lens of adversarial training. A novel type of adversarial training method, termed directional adversarial training (DAT), is introduced. In DAT, a training example is modified in the direction of another example while retaining its original label as the target for training. It is demonstrated that MixUp can be viewed as a specific instance of DAT, sharing the same expected loss function and aligning with the same optimization problem in the long run. This insight not only elucidates why MixUp works effectively but also identifies a broader category of MixUp techniques, known as Untied MixUp. The research shows that Untied MixUp methods are equivalent to all DAT schemes. Empirical evidence supports the existence of Untied MixUp variants that outperform MixUp.

Shadows dance on the wall as overhead lights sway to an unfelt breeze. The din of my team's work is now drowned by the mass of earth and structure between us. It is cool in this dark hall. I scrape against the wall as I push further inwards, away from the lazy lights. I shuffle on, driven. I hear something. It is faint, a gentle whisper bouncing through the passageway. It beckons me. With each step the whisper grows. It is neither urgent nor is it aloof. It simply is, and I must heed it. The sounds brush past me, against me, and into me. I hear it. Human voices. Uncountable, indistinguishable. The passage has ended. There is no light behind me, though I have only walked straight. The wall before me is as smooth as the surface of water. I brush the back of my hand against it. It clings to me, as do the whispers. My very essence trembles as I caress the wall and swim amongst the sea of hushed voices. The surface shifts, and the whispers begin to slip away into the otherworldly smoothness. As they depart my thoughts trickle back. I am afraid. I am alone. I need help. The last of the whispers sink into the surface. I press against it, overcoming my fear so that I may understand this place. Beyond the wall the hushed chorus continues its song. I push harder against the impossibly smooth wall, straining to hear a word amongst the multitude beyond it. It as if the whispers are the heart of humanity, afraid and crowded together in this deep and lonesome dark. The voices are the time-lost echoes of every utterance of man: each roar of might, every love-soaked lament, every plea. I pull away from the wall with a start. Amid the whirlwind words I heard only one. A single word made from the countless voices of humanity, the amalgam of our timeless tongues, the essence of our existence: " Help. "

The concept environmental determinism served as a moral justification for domination of certain territories and peoples. It was believed that a certain person's behaviours were determined by the environment in which they lived and thus validated their domination. For example, people living in tropical environments were seen as "less civilized" therefore justifying colonial control as a civilizing mission. Across the three waves of European colonialism (first in the Americas, second in Asia and lastly in Africa), environmental determinism was used to categorically place indigenous people in a racial hierarchy. This takes two forms, orientalism and tropicality.

At the time George Washington became president in 1776, he served only for two terms. There was no legal restriction preventing him from serving a third term, and he chose to step down after two terms. This decision set a precedent for subsequent presidents, who also opted for limited terms. No law existed at that time prohibiting a president from serving more than two terms; it was simply a matter of convention. Franklin D. Roosevelt was the first to break this norm, and most politicians did not object. Concerns arose later about the potential for a single individual to rule the country, leading to the adoption of the 22nd Amendment, which limits presidential terms to a maximum of two. As a result, presidents today are restricted to a maximum of two terms, or eight years.

We propose a compressive sensing algorithm that exploits geometric properties of images to recover images of high quality from few measurements. The image reconstruction is done by iterating the two following steps: 1) estimation of normal vectors of the image level curves and 2) reconstruction of an image fitting the normal vectors, the compressed sensing measurements and the sparsity constraint. The proposed technique can naturally extend to non local operators and graphs to exploit the repetitive nature of textured images in order to recover fine detail structures. In both cases, the problem is reduced to a series of convex minimization problems that can be efficiently solved with a combination of variable splitting and augmented Lagrangian methods, leading to fast and easy-to-code algorithms. Extended experiments show a clear improvement over related state-of-the-art algorithms in the quality of the reconstructed images and the robustness of the proposed method to noise, different kind of images and reduced measurements.

Where a restaurant's pizza quality can range from amazing to average, frozen pizza ranges from average to inedible. There is no overlap; even the very best frozen pizza isn't as good as a mediocre pizzeria pie. So why eat frozen pizza? If you don't want to cook, or you've run out of other food, and you're prepared to eat an average pizza, then it's probably better to order a pizza than eat a frozen one. Frozen pizza is the last resort of the hungry or uninspired. It's hard to find good frozen pizza, but it's not impossible. The big three frozen pizza brands are DiGiorno, Tombstone, and Totino's, and although all three of these are owned by the same company (Nestle), only DiGiorno really produces good pizza. DiGiorno pizzas are basically the same as their restaurant line, with the same thin crust and high quality ingredients. The biggest difference is the shape: restaurant pizzas are round, while frozen pizzas are square. If you like the restaurant pizzas but don't want to cook, then try the frozen DiGiorno's. They're definitely worth the extra money.

The ISOIEC JPEG 2000 image coding standard is a family of source coding algorithms targeting high-resolution image communications. JPEG 2000 features highly scalable embedded coding features that allow one to interactively zoom out to reduced resolution thumbnails of enormous data sets or to zoom in on highly localized regions of interest with very economical communications and rendering requirements. While intended for fixed-precision input data, the implementation of the irreversible version of the standard is often done internally in floating point arithmetic. Moreover, the standard is designed to support high-bit-depth data. Part 2 of the standard also provides support for three-dimensional data sets such as multicomponent or volumetric imagery. These features make JPEG 2000 an appealing candidate for highly scalable communications coding and visualization of two- and three-dimensional data produced by scientific simulation software. We present results of initial experiments applying JPEG 2000 to scientific simulation data produced by the Parallel Ocean Program (POP) global ocean circulation model, highlighting both the promise and the many challenges this approach holds for scientific visualization applications.

The process of collecting and annotating training data may introduce distribution artifacts which may limit the ability of models to learn correct generalization behavior. We identify failure modes of SOTA models that result from distributional shifts in training data, and suggest methods to improve their robustness to distributional shifts. One approach is to use data augmentation techniques that introduce random variations to the training data, such as random cropping, rotation, and flipping. Another approach is to use adversarial training, where the model is trained to resist perturbations to its input data. Additionally, it is important to carefully monitor and evaluate the performance of the model on new data, such as cross-validation, to ensure that it has learned the correct generalization behavior.

Researchers examined three regions in England at different times and observed that current rates of dementia are lower than previously predicted. They attribute this decline to improved men's health. However, charities caution against relaxation, noting over 200,000 new dementia cases are diagnosed annually in the UK. The study involved interviewing approximately 7,500 individuals aged 65 and older from Cambridgeshire, Nottingham, and Newcastle in the early 1990s, followed by a repeat assessment two decades later. The researchers noted stable new dementia cases among women during this period but a decrease in men. Extending these results to the entire UK, they estimate 40,000 fewer dementia cases compared to earlier projections. While scientists remain uncertain about the exact cause, they suggest men may be improving their health habits, including reduced smoking, lower sodium intake, increased physical activity, and better management of hypertension. They acknowledge that similar trends might not apply to women but hypothesize men could be catching up on health advancements women have already experienced. Nevertheless, they emphasize that factors like rising obesity and diabetes could counteract this trend in the future. Professor Carol Brayne of the University of Cambridge stated, "I am cautiously optimistic that things are stabilizing, but without continued improvements in health, we may see an increase in dementia cases with aging populations. This is a form of cautious optimism." Scientists highlight that dementia is not necessarily unavoidable and can be mitigated through better health practices, urging the need for enhanced public health initiatives.

He craned his bony neck as he stared off into the distance, searching for the soul he was meant to guide to the underworld. Suddenly, a faint shimmer caught his eye, and he pushed the oar downwards to stop the boat. As the boat skidded to a halt, a shape slowly began to emerge from the mist. It was the figure of a young woman with long dark hair and a white gown. Charon raised a skeletal hand to signal her to come closer. The woman stepped onto the boat, her bare feet making no sound as she settled onto the bench opposite Charon. Without a word, she handed him a gold coin, the payment necessary for passage across the river. Charon nodded in acknowledgement and pushed off from the shore, dipping the oar back into the dark waters. As the boat glided across the river, the woman peered into the murky depths, her gaze distant and unfocused. Charon broke the silence, his gravelly voice echoing out across the waters. "Why do you seek Hades, young one?" The woman's gaze traveled from the water to Charon's skull, her eyes unreadable. "I seek my love," she whispered, her voice barely audible over the sounds of the waves. Charon nodded slowly, understanding the depth of her sorrow. For though he was the ferryman of souls, he knew all too well the pain of loss. Together they continued on the journey to the underworld, the silence holding space for the woman's grief.

I awoke abruptly in my bunk aboard the pirate ship. It was pitch black, the only light coming from a few stars that shone through the porthole window. I heard nothing but the gentle lapping of the waves against the hull. Confused, I sat up and looked around. Where had everyone gone? The ship should have been bustling with activity but instead it was eerily still. I shivered as I climbed out of my bunk and stumbled down the hallway in search of answers. The further I went, the more my confusion grew. There was not a soul to be seen, yet the ship seemed to be filled with an unearthly presence. A chill ran down my spine as I reached the main deck. The sight that met my eyes was unlike anything I had ever seen before. The deck was painted with blood, yet there were no corpses or any other signs of violence. It appeared as if the crew had simply vanished without a trace. Fear gripped me as I raced back to my bunk in hopes of finding some clues. But all I found was a piece of parchment with one word written on it: "Run." My heart raced as I realized what must have happened. Someone had come aboard while I slept and taken the entire crew captive. I must have been the only one left behind. I scrambled to the wheelhouse and took control of the vessel. I knew I had to get away as quickly as possible before whoever had done this returned. I steered the ship into the night, sailing away from whatever horrors had befallen those who came before me. As I left the cursed vessel behind, I vowed never to forget the sight of the bloody deck and the fate of its former crew.

In this paper, we present a model-based frequency controller for microgrids with nonzero line resistances based on a port-Hamiltonian formulation of the microgrid model and real-time dynamic pricing. The controller is applicable for conventional generation with synchronous machines as well as for power electronics interfaced sources and it is robust against power fluctuations from uncontrollable loads or volatile regenerative sources. The price-based formulation allows additional requirements such as active power sharing to be met. The capability and effectiveness of our procedure is demonstrated by means of an 18-node exemplary grid.

As soon as I enter the sanctuary I knew something is wrong. There are no flowers. There is no music. There is no casket. And there are only a handful of individuals standing at the front of the room, though I know every single one. They're all solemnly chuckling at something, and I hear a low murmur of " Carlos... " As I approach the group another figure I haven't noticed emerges from the shadows, back straight and suit crisp. Nodding to me he says, " Now that you're all here we can begin. First of all, I would like to apologize for drawing you all here under somewhat... less than honest circumstances. " Less than honest? I look down at the ornately decorated card I hold at my side. What on earth is going on? I am about to speak up, but a voice from the past beats me to it. " Look here. I don't know who you think you are, but where I come from you could have gotten a serious beating for something like this. Why, at my old school... " Another voice cuts in, and I turn to see Ralphie stalk up to the man and grab him by his collar. " Where is Miss Frizzle?? " Calm as ever, he looks my old friend in the eye and said, " Oh, she's dead. There was never any doubt about that. Follow me please. " Ralphie's hand drops to his side as the man disappears down a side hallway. We all glance at each other before reaching a silent agreement and following. He leads us to a small room lined with books and furnished only by a small wooden desk. On it sits an old TV attached to a beat-up DVD player. He settles into the chair next to the desk and picked up a remote control. " I suppose I should explain. I am Miss Frizzle's attorney. She gave me explicit instructions that upon her death I should gather you eight and... I'll let her explain the rest. " With that he presses a button, and the screen brightens to reveal a face that causes my heart to swell even after all these years. Her face holds more creases than I remember, but the mischievous glint is still firmly lodged in her eyes. As her gaze sweeps across the room I could almost swear she's looking us all right in the face, and as she looks at me a faint smile creases her lips. Clearing her throat, she speaks. " Hello class. If you are all watching this, I am dead. Which means that it worked! " She pauses, clearly letting her words sink in before continuing. " I have had many adventures over the years, and explored many exciting and wonderful places. But as I get older, I realize that there is one facet of our life and our existence that I have never explored. So I have decided to see what awaits us after our mortal bodies expire. And to do that... Well, here we are. " The gravity of what she is saying hits me all at once, and my vision blurs as my eyes brim with tears. From the shuffling and a whispered, " Oh bad, oh bad.... " around me, I'm not the only one. After a moment the voice of my mentor breaks through the fog. " BUT! I realized there was a problem. Once I'm... wherever I'm going to end up, there is no way for me to return. On my own, that is. I'm going to need help, and it when it comes down to it, it was always you eight. So what do you say? I can't guarantee you'll return. But I'd love it if you'd join me one last time to take chances, make mistakes, and, well, you know the drill. See you on the other side... " I look up in time to see a glitch in the recording cause her dress to flare, and then the screen goes dark. My mouth is hanging open, and I know it's not the only one. Everyone in the room is trying to process the impossible, and failing rather miserably. The lawyer in the room clears his throat as he stands and holds out his hand. " I have been instructed to entrust you with these. " I realize that no one is moving. We are all rooted to our spots like trees soaking in sunlight to make food. Basking in the charge given us by possibly the most important person of our young lives. Of our lives. I look around at the faces surrounding me. One and all, we learned about our world, our lives, and ourselves from this woman and her magical love of knowledge. And I know what I must do. I step forward and lift the keys from his palm. " Very good, sir. " I am about to turn to address my classmates when our teacher's face appears back on the screen. " She's parked around back, Arnold. " She winks and disappears. I can't help but laugh out loud. Tim joins me, followed by Dorothy Ann and Wanda, and soon we are all doubled over, back in grade school again chasing this wonderful woman through time and space. NASA Is Going to Test Drive an Alien-Hunting Robot in Antarctica NASA will soon be testing an innovative robot designed to hunt for signs of alien life in Antarctica. The robot is equipped with some of the most advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and autonomous navigation. The robot, named Zoe (short for " Zodiacal Exploration and Observation " ), is part of the NASA Mars Sample Return program, which aims to automate the search for microbial life on Mars. According to Johannes Jansen, a research scientist at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, "Zoe is our best hope for discovering extraterrestrial life." He added that the robot is equipped with the latest scientific instruments that allow it to detect even the smallest traces of life. The mission in Antarctica is critical for Zoe, as it will be exposed to harsh conditions that are similar to those expected on Mars. The robot is equipped with a range of sensors, including high-definition (HD) cameras, spectrometers, and a variety of other sensors that will enable it to record data on the surrounding environment. "The Antarctic terrain is the closest environment on Earth that resembles the conditions on Mars. By testing Zoe there, we'll be able to gather critical data that will be essential in designing missions to Mars," explains Jansen. The robot also has two main objectives during its test run in Antarctica. First, Zoe will scout the area to identify potential landing sites for future missions. Second, the robot will work together with a team of scientists to collect data on the composition of the soil, the temperature, and other environmental factors. NASA plans to launch Zoe on its official mission to Mars in the near future, and the Antarctica test run is a crucial step towards the success of the program. If all goes according to plan, Zoe could uncover groundbreaking discoveries and pave the way for further explorations into the unknown depths of our universe.

In the Hautes-Alpes region, livestock are being fed beneath ski lifts on slopes that are set to be covered by heavy snowfall. However, this year, the ability to roam freely has been restricted. In the dense forest areas, a gray wolf is actively hunting. Once nearly driven to extinction in France during the 1930s, the wolf has since been safeguarded as an endangered species and is experiencing a remarkable resurgence. Approximately 200 wolves have established themselves in the southern parts of France, divided into roughly 20 packs. These wolves are believed to have migrated from Italy in the 1990s and are now moving further north. Lionel Serres has 250 sheep on the mountainside this summer, with each night requiring them to be penned behind electric fences. Despite the wolf's cleverness, it has already killed 17 of his female sheep, with 10 more missing. Sheep have become increasingly spooked. On the day they met, Lionel was working to retrieve an ewe that had been caught by a wolf around its neck. The wool was matted and covered in blood. "We've experienced numerous deaths and injuries among our flock," he stated. "Some are lame, others are anxious, and a few have miscarried lambs." At night, the wolf circulates the enclosures until the sheep jump over the electric barriers. These losses are becoming too costly, prompting Lionel to hire an additional shepherd to stay with the sheep overnight. This issue is not unique to him; nearby farmers are also concerned, leading to large signs along the road to Hautes-Alpes, near the border with Italy, reading "NO to the wolf." Although 200 wolves may seem insignificant, this season has seen nearly 600 attacks resulting in the death of over 2,000 sheep. This represents a 20% increase compared to the previous year. Under pressure from farmers and facing a growing number of attacks, the local prefect has finally ordered a search for a single wolf suspected of causing the incidents.

Following the defeat of Japan in the Second World War, anti-Japanese resistance movements in Malaya turned their attention towards the British, who had moved to quickly retake control of the colony, valuing it as a source of rubber and tin. The fact that the guerrillas were primarily Malayan-Chinese Communists meant that the British attempt to quell the uprising was supported by the Muslim Malay majority, on the understanding that once the insurgency had been quelled, independence would be granted. The Malayan Emergency, as it was called, began in 1948 and lasted until 1960, but by 1957, Britain felt confident enough to grant independence to the Federation of Malaya within the Commonwealth. In 1963, the 11 states of the federation together with Singapore, Sarawak and North Borneo joined to form Malaysia, but in 1965 Chinese-majority Singapore was expelled from the union following tensions between the Malay and Chinese populations. Brunei, which had been a British protectorate since 1888, declined to join the union and maintained its status until independence in 1984.

In a historic partnership, NASA has chosen Axiom Space to build the first-ever commercial module for the International Space Station (ISS). The decision is part of NASA's plan to expand the commercial sector's role in space exploration. Axiom Space is a Houston-based startup on a mission to "make living and working in space possible for all." The company was founded in 2016 by former NASA astronaut Michael Suffredini, who served as ISS Program Manager for a decade. Under the agreement, Axiom will build and launch a habitable module that will attach to the space station's Node 2 Forward port. The module will provide commercial facilities for research, manufacturing, and creating additional living space for astronauts. NASA has not specified a timeline for the launch, but Axiom is expected to provide more details soon. This collaboration is part of NASA's Commercial LEO Development (CLD) program, which aims to foster commercial activity in low-Earth orbit (LEO). The program has a budget of 140 million, and Axiom will receive some of that funding as part of its agreement with NASA. This is a major milestone for Axiom Space and the entire commercial space sector. It represents a significant shift in the way NASA operates, as the space agency seeks to leverage the growing capabilities of private companies to achieve its goals. Axiom's module will help pave the way for other commercial habitats and will enable the United States to maintain a presence in LEO for decades to come. The commercial space market is rapidly growing, and NASA's partnership with Axiom Space is just the beginning. As the private sector continues to invest in space exploration, we can expect more partnerships like this to emerge, driving innovation and progress in this exciting new frontier.

The two-page note, addressed to Mrs Ellis and dated 19 August 1945, finds him dealing with the subject of joy. It was found by its owner in a copy of Lewis's book, A Problem of Pain, bought years before. Auctioneer Chris Albury said "keen interest worldwide" had boosted the guide price from PS1,500. Dominic Winter Auctioneers in South Cerney said the letter had been bought by a private buyer from California. "It's a wonderful, thoughtful letter by one of the most highly regarded English writers of the 20th Century," Mr Albury said. "Any original and unpublished letter that gives new insights into a collectable writer's ideas is going to have an appeal, and this one has literary, autobiographical, philosophical and theological content, so ticks every box. "The letter was written just days after Japan's surrender at the end of the Second World War and perhaps the idea of joy, which he thought very unlike pleasure, was once again on his mind." In the letter, which is in "very good" condition, Lewis writes: "Real joy.... jumps under one's ribs and tickles down one's back and makes one forget meals and keeps one (delightedly) sleepless o' nights. "It shocks one awake when the other (security and prosperity) puts one to sleep. "My private table is one second of joy is worth 12 hours of pleasure." Mr Albury said the subject of joy was a "continual theme" throughout Lewis's life. "Interesting, too, is the fact that he was to meet and marry a woman called Joy a few years later," he said.

I'm currently watching the Clone Wars television series and for the life of me: Darth Sidious' plans to create the empire are fucking convoluted, the basis of the Clone War is mind-bogglingly stupid. George Lucas had no idea about writing interesting political intrigue and in the end we got what we got. I'd also argue that, aside from Empire, the original trilogy is plodding, and butchered by Lucas' continuous edits through the 90'searly 2000's. Putting aside the criticisms of the quality of the separate films, together they make a terrible basis for Star Wars canon anyway: because Lucas basically flew by the seat of his pants in creating the series, there are various issues that make the whole of the canon nonsensical (Obi Wan not recognizing C3P0, the new trilogy turning Han Solo into the equivalent of a climate change denier for not believing in the force, advanced technology like R2's rockets and electricity just up and disappear, midichlorians, etc.). Obviously, Lucas created some timeless characters and concepts that will always stoke the imaginations of fantasy fans the world over, but the context in which those concepts exist is just a muddy, lifeless quagmire. A Song of Ice and FireGame of Thrones has shown how amazingly interesting political intrigue can be - it's also shown how to handle a array of characters while making them human, interesting, and understandable in their own right. The property also handled the emergence of magic (somewhat like the resurgence of force-weilders in the original trilogy) in a way that is mysterious and entrancing. Applying that level of attention to detail to the Star Wars universe is the true way to improve the property: Not continuing to build on the shaky foundation left by Lucas. TL;DR: Reducing the canon of Star Wars to the filmsClone Wars tv series hasn't increased clarity of the continuity, and in fact has removed the vast majority of actual entertaining media in the canon to about 1.5 films. The rich history and imagination-capturing concepts like light sabers, the Jedi, the Sith, etc. are all begging to be retold in a way free from the shackles of hack-y, schtick-y robots, inane nonsensical plot-points, terrible writing, bad acting and continuity errors. Years ago, keyboards used distinct pin configurations to represent each bit of information. When certain keys were pressed, specific pins carried voltage differently from others. USB operates differently; it transmits data bit by bit, swiftly, akin to networking. Holding multiple keys results in transmitting more bytes. Audio recording involves converting sound into digital data and sending it directly to the computer. Professional audio is captured at least 44,100 samples per second, with 24 bits per sample, resulting in a data rate of approximately 1060 kbps. USB 2 supports up to 480 Mbps, equivalent to about 47 microphones operating simultaneously. USB functions as a high-speed serial communication system, sending two bits per pin and rapidly switching between them. This rapid switching occurs millions of times per second, sufficient for audio processing. The ability to detect numerous key presses and capture high-quality audio stems from the USB device acting as a small computer. It processes inputs, records audio, and packages data into a single bitstream, which is transmitted via the USB connection. Data is sent only over two out of four pins, while the other two handle power delivery. Microphones can transmit audio nearly in real-time because sound waves change air pressure rapidly, unlike computers. High-pitched sounds involve frequent air pressure changes, reaching up to 20,000 cycles per second. A microphone captures these changes, converting them into digital data for recording.

Deep convolutional neural network-based object detection and recognition algorithms typically require substantial computational power to implement. This poses a specific challenge for embedded systems, like mobile robots, where available computing resources are limited compared to those found in workstations. To address this, we propose employing foveated image sampling instead of standard uniformly sampled images. Foveated sampling reduces image size, leading to faster processing in CNNs due to fewer convolution operations. We tested object detection and recognition on the Microsoft COCO dataset using foveated image sampling at varying resolutions, from 416×416 to 96×96 pixels, on an embedded GPU—NVIDIA Jetson TX2 equipped with 256 CUDA cores. The results indicate that achieving a 4-fold increase in frame rate is feasible, rising from 3.59 FPS to 15.24 FPS when using 416×416 and 128×128 pixel images. For foveated sampling, the reduction in image size resulted in only a slight decline in recall performance within the foveal region, maintaining 92.0% of the baseline performance with full-sized images, whereas uniformly sampled images experienced a much more pronounced drop in recall performance, reaching 50.1% of the baseline level. This highlights the benefits of foveated sampling.

Given the increasing complexity of many sociotechnical work domains, effective teamwork is becoming more and more crucial. While face-to-face communication contributes to effective teamwork, understanding the time-varying nature and structure of team communication is limited. In this work, we combine sensor-based social analytics of Sociometric badges (Rhythm Badge) with two visualization techniques (Dynamic Complexity Heat Maps and Network Visualizations) in order to advance an intuitive way of understanding the dynamics of team interaction. To demonstrate the utility of our approach, we provide a case study that examines one team's interaction for a Lost at Sea simulation. Our results show that we are able to recover transitions in the task and in the team interaction. Not only this, but we uncover structural changes in the energy and engagement of team members and visualize these in networks. Taken together, this work represents an important first step at identifying critical transitionsevents in team communication and interaction patterns that form the basis for many promising future studies focused on optimizing team performance and well-being.

In recent years, numerous vehicular technologies, e.g., cruise control and steering assistant, have been proposed and deployed to improve the driving experience, passenger safety, and vehicle performance. Despite the existence of such vehicular technology, a significant number of road accidents still occur, which are caused by human errors such as lack of attentiveness or distraction. As human errors will not disappear in the near future, a large number of automation systems have been developed to reduce human errors and increase the safety level of vehicular systems. Connected vehicles are expected to further improve the safety level of vehicular systems by using advanced communication and sensing technologies. However, the realization of connected vehicles is constrained by the limited capacity and high cost of wireless communication, which can cause wireless signal collision. Connected vehicle communication is usually referred to as Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication. V2V communication is the direct communication between vehicles or between a vehicle and the roadside infrastructure. V2V communication provides a number of applications to enhance the safety of vehicular systems. For example, V2V communication can be used for collision warning, blind spot detection, intersection collision warning, and lane departure warning. In addition, V2V communication is also used for the coordination of platooning, which can significantly improve the energy efficiency of vehicular systems. V2I communication is the communication between a vehicle and the roadside infrastructure. V2I communication is mainly used for traffic management. For example, V2I communication can be used to provide traffic information to vehicles to improve their traveling experience and driving efficiency. The demand for automation and communication technologies is increasing rapidly in the field of vehicular systems. In particular, V2V and V2I communication technologies have significant impacts on vehicular systems. Consequently, a number of international standardization organizations and research institutions are focusing on the development of V2V and V2I communication standards and technologies. However, existing V2V and V2I communication standards are mainly focused on the definition of communication protocols. In addition, they do not pay sufficient attention to the security issues in vehicular networks. The need for V2V and V2I communication security has been emphasized in recent years. The security of V2V and V2I communication networks is critical to the development of connected vehicles. A compromised vehicle can affect the safety and performance of connected vehicles. In particular, a compromised vehicle can be used to launch attacks on other vehicles, resulting in a large number of road accidents and loss of human lives. A large number of researchers have recognized the importance of security in vehicular networks. They have proposed various V2V and V2I security protocols to protect the confidentiality and integrity of communications between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. In this book chapter, we review the state-of-the-art in vehicular network security. We first review the existing standards for V2V and V2I communication. We then review the existing security protocols for V2V and V2I communication. We analyze the security issues and threats in V2V and V2I networks and provide a number of solutions to tackle such threats. We also highlight the importance of V2V and V2I communication security. The chapter can be used as a guideline for the development of secure V2V and V2I communication standards.

August seventh. The first thing I said to her. "I've been a regular here for over five years, I'm surprised I've never seen you before. You new?" I knew she was, of course. I'm an observant guy and this girl still had all the tell tale signs of workplace training wheels: she'd glance at the menu for price listings and she hadn't nailed the server's technique of carrying plates, also her uniform was clean, too clean. Small details that gave her away. She smiled and nodded quite eagerly. "Yep, only been two days so far. Is it that obvious?" "No, no. I'm only mentioning it because I come here so often, that's all." There was a persistent levity in her voice, like she was constantly mulling over and enjoying the punch line to a good joke. It made her smile so readily, too. I liked that; people don't smile enough these days. I pointed up towards the boards. "I'll take a number twelve - with black tea and toast, thanks." She was quick to scribble my order down onto a pad. I waited and watched the end of her pen dance around in frantic movements. The girl then looked back up and gestured towards a nearby table. "Sure thing, that will be right out," she said. The cafe was empty, which is probably why I did something quite uncharacteristic for me: I stayed at the counter, to chat. I don't dislike people, I just grow tired of them every once in a while, so normally I'm content to read the paper in peace. But on that day, I chose to chat to the new girl. Perhaps this was because she was beautiful and in some small, repressed part of me, I harboured a hope that she'd like me too. God, I hope I'm not that sentimental. "So, what's that accent? I can't place it and I'm normally great at placing them." I'd hopped onto the next topic hastily, just trying to keep her interested. She seemed more than happy to talk and her face lit up under the greasy morning light. "Yeah, sorry. It's a bit of mish-mash. I'm originally from England, but I've spent a bunch of time travelling around the world. Here and there." "Japan wouldn't happen to be on that list would it? Or Asia, anyway." "No, Japan's correct. How did you know?" "Just a hunch. The way you hold the kettle, it's a little more..... eh, reverent." A lucky guess and late night documentary was the real answer - but I'd protect that secret for now. She seemed impressed and as ashamed as I am to admit it, I felt a flutter in my stomach. Like anyone who encounters a magician during their off-time, she pressed me for more'tricks.' "You learned that from the way I make tea? That's amazing. I don't suppose you could solve anything else?" "Solve?" "You are a detective, aren't you?" "Is it that obvious?" We laughed and I fell further into her eyes. "Look," she said, seeming to suddenly arrive with an idea. "How about you help me out with one of the puzzles in the paper?" She hurried off before I had a chance to respond; to retrieve the Guardian or whatever publication she read. I drummed an absent tune on the counter-top and glanced outside. On the pavement, the rain was drying, shepherded into small grimy puddles and the clouds above were parting like foam, dragged back by the blue tide. Looked like it might be an all right day, after all. A flat slapping sound brought my attention back to the counter, where the girl had chucked a newspaper down, open to the crosswords and puzzles page. She wore a big, white grin. "There you go,'officer.' See how you fare with that. I've almost finished it, but I couldn't get the last ones." I felt a bit like a performing monkey, but I let it slide and promptly plucked a red ballpoint out from a pot beside the till. Scanning the black and white spread, I could see where she'd started and ultimately given up; her efforts had been scratched on in blue biro. "I'll just get your food. Be right back." My first instincts. She was really bad at these. I smiled quietly, noting a couple of easy corrections, blaring up from the page. Cute, but incorrect. I started to etch over her writings, inputting the correct answers where I could figure them out. "You're really bad at this!" "I know! I'm terrible!" I could picture her back in the kitchen, a laugh so near to her lips. I continued to work down the page finishing off the crossword in seconds. 'Communal gathering outside PARK' 'Verb of vehicular movement DRIVE' 'Month named after the first Roman Emperor AUGUST' Then, I realized she'd gotten a few of the sudoku numbers wrong, so I amended them too. A 9 and a 5 in one box. A 7 in another. "They're done. You left the easy ones! How's it going back there?" I pursed my lips, waiting - and waiting. Soon, when she still hadn't replied, I craned up upon my tiptoes, trying to peek round into the kitchen. "Hey, Miss? Are you okay?" Suddenly my mobile started to buzz in my pocket. I forgot about the situation in the cafe and quickly snatched for my phone. I'd been expecting a call. "Hayson speaking, got news for me?" The voice on the other end of the line was slow to reply, bogged down by reluctance. "Christian, you're not going to like this "What?" "There's been another one." I held myself upright, but only barely. I felt sick and my free hand flew to my brow, wiping at stressed creases. "Are you fucking serious? But we had the Marston kid locked up!" "Yeah, no shit. You know what that means "That he didn't do it. I know. I know, I know, but fucking hell, Sawyer. Fucking shit. This is I exhaled heavily and sagged back onto an empty table. "Alright," I said. "Tell me the address and I'll be there shortly." "Sure thing, Chris. It's ninety-five, Park Drive." My lips opened, but whatever had been about to escape them was suddenly torn back down my throat. My eyes shot towards the newspaper that lay goading on the counter-top. Sawyer was speaking into my ear but I wasn't listening. I darted across and stared with disbelief at the spread. My handiwork was scarred over the page in bright red ink: PARK DRIVE 95 AUGUST 7. I'd encountered coincidences before, but this time I knew - I knew it was no random glitch of fate. "Miss!?" In seconds I was shouting, stretched over the counter and bellowing into the kitchen, but no one replied. The kettle, still on the hob, began to scream and screech, joining my voice in cluttering the cafe. Who the fuck was that waitress? This little parlour trick, she couldn't seriously have pulled all of this off? Could she? I dropped the phone, clutching my scalp with both hands. I felt hot, impossibly hot. In desperation I searched around the room, finally falling upon the one thing I should have noticed. As observant as I claimed to be, I looked to the door, only to see the letters'OPEN' staring back at me. The cafe had been closed all along. I don't know if this answers the prompt or not. It was just another ordinary day when Jake found himself at the police station being interrogated about a murder that he didn't commit. He had no idea what they were talking about until they showed him the evidence. A surveillance video clearly showed him walking out of the victim's apartment building around the same time of the murder. Jake was in shock. He couldn't believe what he was seeing. He had no recollection of being at the victim's apartment, let alone killing them. As the investigation progressed, more evidence piled up against Jake. His fingerprints were found on the murder weapon and on the door handle to the victim's apartment. But how could this be? Jake had never seen the victim before, let alone been to their apartment. The more the evidence pointed towards Jake, the more he began to question his own sanity. Had he blacked out and committed this terrible crime without even realizing it? Days turned into weeks, and the trial was fast approaching. Jake was wracked with guilt and confusion. He couldn't shake the feeling that somehow, he had been responsible for the murder, even though he had no memory of doing so. Finally, it was time for the trial. The prosecution presented their case, and Jake's defense team did their best to refute the evidence. But in the end, it wasn't enough. The jury found Jake guilty of the murder, and he was sentenced to life in prison. Years passed, and Jake had resigned himself to a life behind bars. But then, a breakthrough came. A new piece of evidence surfaced, proving that someone else had committed the murder - not Jake. The courts quickly overturned his conviction, and Jake was a free man once again. But the weight of the guilt that he had carried for so many years stayed with him. In the end, he knew that although he may not have consciously committed the murder, somehow, in some way, he was still responsible.

This paper introduces Minimalist Transfer Learning (MinTL) to streamline the design process for task-oriented dialogue systems and reduce reliance on annotated data. MinTL is a straightforward yet effective transfer learning framework that enables the integration of pre-trained seq2seq models and facilitates the joint learning of dialogue state tracking and response generation. Different from prior methods that utilize a copy mechanism to propagate old dialogue states, we introduce Levenshtein belief spans (L e v), enabling efficient dialogue state tracking with minimal generation length. Our framework is implemented using two pre-trained backbones—T5 and BART—and is evaluated on MultiWOZ. Experimental results show that: 1) our systems attain novel state-of-the-art performance on end-to-end response generation; 2) MinTL-based systems outperform baselines in low-resource settings, achieving competitive results with just 20 training examples; and 3) L e v significantly enhances inference speed.

Namibia (inmbi, n, officially the Republic of Namibia (German: Republik Namibia (helpinfo); Afrikaans: Republiek van Namibie) is a country in southern Africa whose western border is the Atlantic Ocean. It shares land borders with Zambia and Angola to the north, Botswana to the east and South Africa to the south and east. Although it does not border Zimbabwe, a part of less than 200 metres of the Zambezi River (essentially a small bulge in Botswana to achieve a BotswanaZambia micro-border) separates it from that country. Namibia gained independence from South Africa on 21 March 1990, following the Namibian War of Independence. Its capital and largest city is Windhoek, and it is a member state of the United Nations (UN), the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the African Union (AU), and the Commonwealth of Nations.

Metagenome assembly is the process of transforming a set of short, overlapping, and potentially erroneous DNA segments from environmental samples into the accurate representation of the underlying microbiomes's genomes. State-of-the-art tools require big shared memory machines and cannot handle contemporary metagenome datasets that exceed Terabytes in size. In this paper, we introduce the MetaHipMer pipeline, a high-quality and high-performance metagenome assembler that employs an iterative de Bruijn graph approach. MetaHipMer leverages a specialized scaffolding algorithm that produces long scaffolds and accommodates the idiosyncrasies of metagenomes. MetaHipMer is end-to-end parallelized using the Unified Parallel C language and therefore can run seamlessly on shared and distributed-memory systems. Experimental results show that MetaHipMer matches or outperforms the state-of-the-art tools in terms of accuracy. Moreover, MetaHipMer scales efficiently to large concurrencies and is able to assemble previously intractable grand challenge metagenomes. We demonstrate the unprecedented capability of MetaHipMer by computing the first full assembly of the Twitchell Wetlands dataset, consisting of 7.5 billion reads - size 2.6 TBytes.

This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of the researches and motivations for hardware implementation of reservoir computing (RC) on neuromorphic electronic systems. Due to its computational efficiency and the fact that it has been successfully implemented on many platforms, RC is considered as one of the most promising algorithms for processing and analyzing high-dimensional, nonlinear and non-stationary data. Recent years have seen a growing interest in the hardware implementation of RC, especially on neuromorphic computing platforms. In this chapter, we provide an overview of the available electronic implementations of RC, including the field-programmable gate array, digital signal processor, application-specific integrated circuit, programmable logic device and neuromorphic system. We also review the most important RC electronic platforms from different perspectives, including the processing element, the number of processing elements, the data type, and the number of layers. Furthermore, we discuss the open research problems and challenges that should be resolved to improve the performance of hardware RC platforms in the future.

The practice of labelling the infringement of exclusive rights in creative works as "piracy" predates statutory copyright law. Prior to the Statute of Anne in 1710, the Stationers' Company of London in 1557, received a Royal Charter giving the company a monopoly on publication and tasking it with enforcing the charter. Those who violated the charter were labelled pirates as early as 1603. The term "piracy" has been used to refer to the unauthorized copying, distribution and selling of works in copyright. Article 12 of the 1886 Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works uses the term "piracy" in relation to copyright infringement, stating "Pirated works may be seized on importation into those countries of the Union where the original work enjoys legal protection." Article 61 of the 1994 Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs) requires criminal procedures and penalties in cases of "willful trademark counterfeiting or copyright piracy on a commercial scale." Piracy traditionally refers to acts of copyright infringement intentionally committed for financial gain, though more recently, copyright holders have described online copyright infringement, particularly in relation to peer-to-peer file sharing networks, as "piracy."

His expensive tailored suit was not very comfortable, and while he supposed he looked good, he felt more at home with less on. Kenji began scanning the crowd. He was certain he would be the biggest and strongest man there, but perhaps someone could pose a challenge. He did not come all the way out here to listen to a stick man speak for some time and to observe strange Americans. The strange man with the large brown coat began moving in the crowd. Kenji's eyes followed the man as he bumped into others, who occasionally muttered and offered mild protests. This paper addresses the problem of target detection and localisation in a limited area using multiple coordinated agents. The swarm of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) determines the position of the targets and reports to an observer on board, who then interprets the data from all sensors and uses this information to estimate various parameters such as the number of active targets within his visual field. There are many applications which can benefit from cooperative sensing systems including surveillance over large areas with low manpower available for monitoring, search and rescue operations where teams conducting reconnaissance missions collaborate to detect threats or find victims, environmental studies that require collaboration between groups of robots performing ground surveys and aerial maps coverage, etc 1. While there has been some research into sensor networks 2, particularly addressing signal processing issues 3, 4, multi-agent coordination 5 and localised state estimation 6, 7, our work focuses exclusively on cooperative perception tasks -the design and implementation of distributed algorithms enabling group decision making and robust consensus formation subject to noisy observations; in particular we consider only problems governed by quadratic cost functions whose objective is to minimise error propagation among cooperating agents. The aim of this study was twofold: first, develop analytical tools to provide insight into how different forms of communication affect performance; secondly, examine the practical feasibility of solving these problems when implemented through agent-based software and hardware platforms. We use the term 'agents' to refer both to individual UAVs equipped with on-board computers andor cameras, but also to other entities capable of communicating via wireless communications devices such as WiFi access points or ad-hoc links 8. To address these objectives we make three contributions related to formal analysis, proof development and algorithm implementations respectively, compared against alternative methods such as game theory 9 and particle filters 10: i) heuristic rules based upon extensive numerical simulations showing improvements in terms of convergence time; ii) formal proofs based on Lyapunov techniques demonstrating boundedness properties; iii) experimental validation of the proposed algorithm in contrasting conditions under which improved results were observed. In Section 2, we present a brief background on solution strategies for linear quadratic optimisation problems arising in cooperative task allocation scenarios. In Sections 3-4, we formulate exact mathematical models capturing key aspects governing the dynamics involving the interaction between heterogeneous agents acting collectively towards common goals. In Section 5 we analyse existing protocols and highlight their shortcomings. Our novel contribution lies in identifying mechanisms allowing more efficient utilisation of resources thereby reducing time-to-solution and thus increasing joint tracking accuracy. By analysing several solutions approaches allowing trade-offs amongst speed, resolution and precision we derive lower bounds, upper bounds and optimality criteria permitting us to choose suitable control laws according to application requirements. Numerical experiments reported in Section 6 demonstrate significant gains achieved by applying this technique, comparing its actual behaviour with standard centralised and decentralised approaches. Finally conclusions drawn in Section 7 summarise and explain why the proposed approach proves effective even in complex real-world environments. We propose a Label Propagation based algorithm for weakly supervised text classification. We construct a graph where each document is represented by a node and edge weights represent similarities among the documents. Additionally, we discover underlying topics using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and enrich the document graph by including the topics in the form of additional nodes. The edge weights between a topic and a text document represent level of "affinity" between them. Our approach does not require document level labelling, instead it expects manual labels only for topic nodes. This significantly minimizes the level of supervision needed as only a few topics are observed to be enough for achieving sufficiently high accuracy. The Label Propagation Algorithm is employed on this enriched graph to propagate labels among the nodes. Our approach combines the advantages of Label Propagation (through document-document similarities) and Topic Modelling (for minimal but smart supervision). We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various datasets and compare with state-of-the-art weakly supervised text classification approaches.

In the year 2245, a new law was passed that every person at the age of 18 must choose an unlikely life event. This event will be the driving force behind the rest of their lives. But there was a catch. If they were to die before their chosen event had occurred, they would be reborn at 18 years old and forced to relive their life over and over again until their event had come to pass. Once that event had occurred, death would become permanent. Many young individuals took this law as a joke and chose their unlikely event haphazardly. But for Francis, it was different. He had put a lot of thought and consideration behind his decision. For years, he had been fascinated with space exploration, and had always dreamt of being the first human to travel to Mars. At 18, Francis confidently picked exploring Mars as his unlikely event. He worked diligently towards his goal, studying physics, mathematics, and space science. In his early 30s, he became an astronaut and eventually, his dream came true. Francis was selected as the head of the first expedition to Mars. During the journey, a powerful solar flare impacted the spacecraft causing a massive explosion, and every one of the crew members died. But Francis was different. He woke up at 18, banged and bruised from the impact, to the realization that he had to start over again from scratch. Francis didn't lose hope; he knew he had to make his Mars dreams come true again. Over the years, Francis had to repeat this process multiple times. With every rebirth, he honed his skills, made better preparations, and became more efficient. With each attempt, his experience and understanding increased. Finally, on his 103rd rebirth, Francis achieved his goal of exploring Mars, and his life's work was fulfilled. Francis's body aged naturally, and he passed away peacefully at the age of 98, knowing that he had fulfilled his unlikely event while achieving one of humanity's greatest accomplishments.

Advances in Web technology enable personalization proxies that assist users in satisfying their complex information monitoring and aggregation needs through the repeated querying of multiple volatile data sources. Such proxies face a scalability challenge when trying to maximize the number of clients served while at the same time fully satisfying clients' complex user profiles. In this work we use an abstraction of complex execution intervals (CEIs) constructed over simple execution intervals (EIs) represents user profiles and use existing offline approximation as a baseline for maximizing completeness of capturing CEIs. We present three heuristic solutions for the online problem of query scheduling to satisfy complex user profiles. The first only considers properties of individual EIs while the other two exploit properties of all EIs in the CEI. We use an extensive set of experiments on real traces and synthetic data to show that heuristics that exploit knowledge of the CEIs dominate across multiple parameter settings.

We analyze the asymptotic stability of the semi-discrete (SD) numerical method used to approximate stochastic differential equations (SDEs). With the rise of cheap small "Cube Satellites," startups are now taking photos and infrared images of factories, retail parking lots, oil tankers, and more and selling these images to customers who want to spy on their competitors, or gain intelligence in other ways. This is not an entirely new phenomenon - the U.S. government has long used satellites to spy on its enemies - but it is becoming increasingly accessible and affordable for private companies and individuals. "It's the democratization of satellite imagery," said Max Chalfin, co-founder and CEO of Terra Bella, a Google subsidiary that sells satellite images to businesses. Terra Bella operates a fleet of seven satellites, each the size of a mini fridge, that circle the Earth every 90 minutes and take high-resolution photos of specific locations that customers request. The company then sells these photos for 1,000 to 5,000 each. Chalfin said the company's customers include oil and gas companies that use the images to track the location of their tankers, retailers that use them to count the number of cars in their competitors' parking lots, and construction companies that use them to track the progress of projects. "People are using this data for all sorts of interesting applications," he said. Another company, Planet Labs, operates a fleet of more than 100 small satellites, called "Doves," that take lower-resolution images of the entire Earth every day. The company sells these images to customers such as farmers, who use them to track the growth of their crops, and mining companies, who use them to track the progress of their operations. "What we're really enabling is a new generation of decision-makers who have access to this data that they never had before," said Will Marshall, co-founder and CEO of Planet Labs. The market for commercial satellite imagery is expected to grow from 2.3 billion in 2015 to 6.7 billion by 2025, according to a report by the research firm MarketsandMarkets. This growth is being driven by the falling cost of launching and operating satellites, as well as the increasing demand for images of Earth from businesses and governments. "It's a very exciting time to be in the satellite industry," said Chalfin.

I purchased the residence in late 2020. It featured a charming neo-gothic design and ample space. Every aspect of the home met my expectations. While I might have considered buying a newer property, this house offered both aesthetic appeal and historical value. I enlisted contractors to handle significant repairs, including rewiring, plumbing, and setting up network infrastructure. However, I aimed to renovate the basement. I was meticulous about workshop configurations and worked closely with the original wooden structures, removing layers of outdated wallpaper and plywood. As I used my crowbar to dismantle the wood panel, I heard a sharp metallic clink. "Oh no, I must have hit a water pipe," I thought. But all the pipes were located on the opposite wall. "Great, this definitely isn't a sewage line," I muttered. Carefully, I maneuvered the crowbar to extract the wood panel, revealing a fearsome elevator. A sophisticated model, yet still a freight elevator. I rushed to my toolset to retrieve a torch and inspect the shaft. I struck the torch against the elevator's cage. "What in heaven's name is this for?" I cautiously pushed the elevator cage door open and tested the car's ability to support my weight. "No groaning. It seems well-lubricated." I slid the gate shut and noticed a single bat passing by. There were two buttons on the control panel; I pressed the lower one. A shudder and smooth movement brought the elevator down. A few moments later, it halted at a metal walkway, illuminated by faint green lights leading nowhere. "Well, this is as far as I'll go. I hope there are lights down here," I said. Feeling along the smooth walls, I discovered a switch and turned it on. Suddenly, I realized what Bruce Wayne did with all his wealth.

The Agency was the subject of [this ethnographic study] (URL0) which details the peculiarities of the IC which impact overall effectiveness. Chief among these peculiarities (not really peculiar as all organizations - government bureaus, large corporations, sports teams, etc, develop their own distinct cultures, mores and languages over time) are: - Extreme insularity. CIA employees set themselves apart from civilian life, see their mission as being of utmost, life-or-death importance (which it is in some cases), and systematically exclude outsiders to the organization. This trickles down to their treatment of new hires, who must "earn" their way up within this rigidly hierarchical and exclusive organization. - An almost hilarious reliance on acronyms and jargon which a) contribute further to the systematic exclusion of outsiders and newbies, b) are employed by veteran personnel to make vague their intentions to others and in doing so further their own personal agendas within the CIA, and c) contributes to the embarrassing overall phenomenon of impenetrable linguistic structures which, when deconstructed, are revealed to be essentially meaningless. For example, the dissertation cites this email subject line: "FYI FOR SA RE: OBE SITREP - NAR AFAIK," which, in IC speak, means "For your information for situational awareness regarding the obsolete situation report - no action required as far as I know." In plain English, this means "nothing happened, no need to do anything." Now, that is pure comedy gold. - Another, related phenomenon is that these linguistic structures bullshit are employed in an atmosphere of extreme interpersonal and professional competitiveness, which leads to what the author depicts as a culture of oneupsmanship. No situation is ever satisfactorily explained as individuals compete with one another to clarify everything said aloud or written until the point where what was originally said is meaningless. Another example, this time of analysts explaining the rules of baseball: "Analyst A: So there are four bases Analyst B: Well, no, it's really three bases plus home plate. Analyst A:.... Okay, three bases plus home plate. The batter hits the ball and advances through the bases one by one - Analyst C: Well, no, it doesn't have to be one base at a time." There's another example in the text of analysts being asked to justify their actions and words endlessly, to the point where "it becomes difficult to say anything definitively without being challenged - often at the expense of the true purpose of the interaction." - One more reason why the IC is dysfunctional is that the job requires effective employees to function as "robots" in order to get through their day. Being repeatedly exposed to violence and carnage and images of violence and carnage, the weight and stakes of the mission and the competitiveness of the organization require analysts to affect an inhuman disposition, which has obvious consequences for people's personal and professional lives. - Information overload, the direct result of so many intelligence pipelines being opened to analysts as a result of post-911 legislation combined with - Stovepiping of intelligence (the separation of information into separate stacks in separate databases) which needlessly complicates the actual acquisition of useful intelligence. In short, the intelligence community suffers from a variety of maladies that hamper its ability to operate effectively, including an exclusive, opaque and purposefully impenetrable professional and social hierarchy, a surfeit of jargon which muddies the waters of personal and professional interaction, a workplace culture where analysts must affect extraordinary stoicness in the face of the absolute worst kinds of violence and stress, and IT practices which are in direct competition with the amount of information they are mandated to sift through. I hope this was helpful and I urge you again to read the paper I cited, because it really is a great peek inside of an organization that very few of us are allowed to be a part of.

In this paper we present a framework for secure identification using deep neural networks, and apply it to the task of template protection for face authentication. We use deep convolutional coding (DSC) as an example to describe the implementation principles of most types of IDF data protection schemes. A target dataset containing faces is also revealed in the randomization process. As shown by an asymmetric algorithm, face recognition may be implemented with multiple architectures and can either expose face information from different types of candidates or provide other forms of identity verification. Targeted masking techniques are used to enhance identity verification and predict which candidate will have the best face. There has been increasing interest in developing high performance modern machine learning algorithms based on error correction technology developed through the intersection between machine learning and security. The general purpose, object classification algorithms (A.P. algorithm) are often used in solving problem learning problems to avoid false positives that could arise due to errors in inference operations. These systems can cause errors concerning the accuracy of matching objects, resulting in incorrect predictions. In contrast to many prior art methods, which rely solely on a pure object classification algorithm, we consider the use of a computational model. To measure convergence, we explore how we implement a single approach by exploring the applicability of a set of large-scale computational models. Using multivariate statistical analysis, we show that a new consensus algorithm, presented with a similarity index of 20, is able to detect the agreement among the A.P. and parallelized concurrency algorithms on average. This results in an additional independent inverse correlation between the two. Our solution provides consistent, low cost efficient optimization solutions suitable for specific applications.

"Ah man, it smells like death in here." That is the phrase that I have lived to regret ever since they fell foolishly from my mouth. I was essentially immortal before that moment in time. I was the best comedian in the world, and apparently better than anyone in the afterlife as well. It was the only reason the Grim Reaper decided not to take me. I could make him laugh, and in his line of work that was a rarity. I don't even remember what it was that I had said when he showed up at my car accident. I can recall him bending down next to my overturned Honda civic and reaching in to pull me out. I made some off the wall comment and he froze, dead in his tracks. It was the weirdest laugh I had ever heard, but one I appreciated more than all of the others combined. He let me live, provided that every year on the anniversary of what should have been my death, I would tell him a joke that would make him cry with laughter. I was his own personal jester, and for that he rewarded me handsomely. And then on that fateful day, 121 years later, I muttered those stupid words that seized our contract and ripped it in two. Who knew Death would be so self conscious about his smell? And to make things worse, that wasn't even the joke that I was going to tell him! The actual joke was a masterpiece, but he wouldn't give me the chance to tell it. I ran out of that room faster than I'd ever run before. And I've been running ever since. I think the reason that he hasn't taken me yet is because of our long history together. That isn't to say that he's forgiven me. He seems to enjoy reminding me that he's near. Everyone I get close to dies without reason. I'll see a dog in the park that I think looks adorable and before I can pet it, it'll fall over dead. Roses crumble before I can enjoy their scent and food rots on my fork before I can bring it to my mouth. He's killing everything around me. I have discovered that Death is a jester of a different sort. I had provided him with a form of humor that he wasn't used to, but he has since grown tired of it, and reverted to his old ways. Now, he once again deals in jokes of cruelty and irony. In a way, I am still fulfilling my part of our old deal. The Reaper still laughs, and he still laughs at me. Only now, the difference is I'm not laughing.
